title: Sunday · Lanes, again
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: The same composition as 2009. Six letters out. The lot empty. The glow on the ridge larger.

panels.composition: Tier 1: SMALL WOOD LANES from across the highway at night, exactly the 2009 framing. Six letters dark: the word is gaps. Rain. The lot empty. No car.

image.prompt: a bowling alley across a two-lane highway at night in wet-on-wet watercolor, its neon sign with six of its letters dark so the name reads as gaps, rain on an empty lot, the same composition as an earlier page
image.notes: Repeat 'Lanes' 2009 Tier 1 exactly; only the sign and the lot differ.

panels.name: The sign

panels.composition: Tier 2: behind. The blue bin where the dumpster was. The rust outline on the gravel. The chain-link. Nothing tied. The bulb.

image.prompt: behind a bowling alley at night: a blue recycling bin on a rust-stained rectangle of gravel, a chain-link fence, a bare bulb, rain, watercolor

panels.name: The outline

panels.composition: Tier 3: wide, later. The sign off. The lot. And on the ridge east of town, the glow — larger than 2009, plainly not the moon, still treated as weather.

image.prompt: the same bowling alley later with its sign dark and the lot empty, and on the forested ridge behind the town a pale glow clearly larger than before and plainly not the moon, still painted like weather, wet-on-wet watercolor, no words

panels.name: The ridge

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet; 2019: the Sunday drawn to a smaller grid
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust; 2020: ochre and slate arriving

notes: 'Lanes' redone ten years on. Six dark. The glow larger.
